summary: Polygon examines how Twitch has become a hub for sports streamers and fans, especially younger audiences, even though broadcast rights keep most major league games off the platform. Streamers like Esfand and Keira Megan work around those limits with watch-alongs, commentary and events, while some leagues have run successful partnerships with streamers. Twitch supports the category with a sports section and a Sports Accelerator Program.
one_line: Twitch has become a popular space for sports commentary and watch-alongs, but broadcast rights limit live games, leaving streamers to build interactive, community-driven sports content.
key_facts: During the COVID-19 shutdowns in 2020, athletes and sports leagues joined Twitch to stream video games while live sports were on hiatus.
WNBA player Aerial Powers streams NBA 2K and Apex Legends, and Sergio Agüero livestreams Kings League and Queens League games on his channel.
Twitch's stand-alone sports category had 2.7 million followers as of publication.
EnterpriseAppsToday reported that Twitch's Sports category registered around 8 million hours of watch time in 2023.
YPulse survey research from April found that 66% of Gen Zers tune into platforms like Twitch to follow their favorite sports.
The NBA signed a deal with Twitch in 2017 to stream minor league games, and a 2019 deal to exclusively stream USA Basketball games globally.
Nielsen reported 13 million total viewers for Amazon's first exclusive Thursday Night Football game, including U.S. Prime Video subscribers who streamed on Twitch.
LiveMode and FIFA partnered with Brazilian streamer Casimito to broadcast the 2022 World Cup on Twitch in Latin America; Casimito also struck a deal to stream the 2023 Women's World Cup.
In 2021 the NBA signed a deal with Alexandre "Gaules" Borba Chiqueta and Budweiser to stream games in Brazilian markets.

Esfand, a streamer with 1.2 million followers, says broadcast rights hinder Twitch from becoming a full-blown sports platform, noting that Canada and most of Europe couldn't watch one of his football streams.
Esfand's Draft Night Extravaganza in April coincided with the first day of the NFL draft and featured Will Neff, Erobb221, Austin Ekeler, Micah Parsons and Kenny Vaccaro.
Esfand's Tailgate Tour showcases college football culture and resonates with young and global fans.
Twitch launched the Sports Accelerator Program to support creators in 'sports talk' such as podcasts, reaction streams and watch-alongs.

Keira Megan (keirameganxx), a U.K.-based streamer focused on soccer and Formula 1, hosts watch-alongs rather than streaming races due to broadcast rights, and says Twitch is where she is most engaged with her audience.
